subject: Post-call: latency ceiling, KV-cache hedges & context capacity recap
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Park <sylvia@veridian.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: latency ceiling, KV-cache hedges & context capacity recap

Thanks again for taking time today, Sylvia — appreciate the deep dive on Veridian's real-time summarization pipeline. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

TL;DR: Veridian needs p95 response <350ms for first stream token on typical 1–2k token requests; concurrency target 120 active users with peaks to 300; typical input size 800 tokens average, worst-case bursts to 6k; output average ~150 tokens.

Notes from the call:
- Latency SLO: target p95 <= 350ms for first-byte/stream start. For full-response tail we discussed softer SLOs (p95 <= 1.2s) given longer generations.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline 120 concurrent sessions; assume 3 requests/min/session average, with burst concurrency up to 300.
- Context window: live summarization keeps ~3k tokens of sliding context in memory. Edge cases can spike to 6k input tokens for long meetings and external docs.
- KV-cache opportunity: we recommended prefix / KV caching for recurring meeting contexts (reduces per-request compute and amortizes KV retrieval). Effective for repeated partial prompts (e.g., meeting transcript windows).
- Hedging & fallbacks: configure routing policy to prefer quantized model variant for background processing; immediate user-facing streaming should hit a higher-throughput low-latency variant, with automatic fallback to a smaller model under capacity pressure.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Large-context spikes (6k) materially increase time to first token if using single-model execution path; we suggested sub-second p95 for first token is feasible only with prefix/KV caching + aggressive batching limits.
- Continuous batching increases throughput but raises tail latency during bursty interactive workloads; recommend conservative batch windows for streaming endpoints.

Attachments: I attached an initial performance matrix with estimated qps/gpu and suggested concurrency knobs (veridian-performance-matrix.xlsx) and a short SOW outline (sow-outline-v1.docx).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Veridian to share a 24-hour sample of request size distribution and a few representative transcripts (anonymized) — helps pin memory and batching parameters.
2) Redwood to run an internal model-matching exercise (quantized vs non-quantized) and provide an estimated p95-first-token and tokens/sec curves. Target deliverable: perf-impacts.pdf by 2027-05-24.
3) Schedule a troika call (Redwood infra + solutions + Veridian eng) to run through KV/cache feasibility and routing policy; proposed window: Tue 2027-05-25 or Wed 2027-05-26.

Questions for your team: could you confirm % of sessions that are live interactive (user waiting for streaming) vs background summarization (async)? That affects batch strategy.

Best,

Jonas Weber

Date: 2027-05-22T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: latency ceiling, KV-cache hedges & context capacity recap

Jonas — quick internal note before we respond to Sylvia.

On KV strategy: propose hybrid approach:
- Per-session KV checkpoints: keep a lightweight key-value prefix every ~1k tokens (or on sentence boundary) so streaming resume + repeated context lookups hit cached KV instead of re-encoding full prefix.
- For long tails >4k, use token-windowing + selective recompute: we materialize only the last 2k into the live compute path; older context becomes part of the cached KV summary vector to reduce attention cost.
- Expected hit-rate: for meeting transcripts with repeated topics/phrases we historically see 40–70% reuse depending on sliding window size (our internal bench). For Veridian, if 65% sessions are interactive and meetings repeat topics, assume 50% hit-rate as conservative.

Operational knobs to control latency:
- Concurrency cap per endpoint (soft limit) + queue length with immediate 'busy' 503 fallback to smaller model variant.
- Short batch windows for streaming (5–10ms) to avoid added first-byte latency.
- Enable preemptive cache-warm on session start when possible.

I'll draft a short one-pager on these hedges that Jonas can send to Sylvia.

Tessa
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: latency ceiling, KV-cache hedges & context capacity recap

Sylvia — quick answers inline, and attaching the perf matrix + SOW outline.

On KV caching approach (short): we recommend per-session prefix checkpoints at ~1k token increments + a light "summary embedding" for older context. That gives two benefits: (1) reduces the attention window for the live path and (2) speeds up first-token because most of the prefix is already encoded. Conservatively we model a ~40–55% end-to-end latency reduction on first-token for cases with repeated context.

Troika call: Tue 2027-05-25 10:00 PT is confirmed on our side — I'll send an invite and include an agenda ( KV mechanics, model variants, routing policy, perf targets + test plan ).

Deliverables: we'll share the model-matching results and a short perf-impacts brief by EOD 5/24. If you can drop the 24-hour sample before then that lets us run a quick sim.

Best,
Jonas
